To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the uncertainty of the rate constant is dominated by uncertainty about the model and uncertainty of other model parameter.

the uncertainty of the kinetic rate constant k(O3) in ozonation is mainly determined by the uncertainty in the model structure and that the transferability of the kinetic rate constants from one system to the other is limited.

k(O3) depends on pH, temperature, and the concentration of natural organic matter (NOM) and that the uncertainty in the prediction of k(O3) at full scale is mainly determined by the uncertainty of k(O3), the uncertainty of other model input parameters, the uncertainty of the model structure, the uncertainty of non-representative samples, and the uncertainty of chemical analysis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the transfer of information in up-scaling and the sources of parameter uncertainty.
the question how to deal with uncertainty in engineering design, and how to improve the reliability and robustness of predictions.
the question of how to obtain a reliable and accurate model for the prediction of treatment performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the uncertainty in the prediction of k(O3) in full scale ozonation is high.

uncertainty in the prediction of treatment performance is determined by a combination of model structure and parameter uncertainty, uncertainty due to sampling and analytical error, and uncertainty due to the upscaling procedure.
uncertainty is a complex and subjective process that is best described by a range of uncertainty estimates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a combination of different experimental setups is necessary to obtain reliable parameter estimates and uncertainty estimates for full scale treatment systems.
the uncertainty of the kinetic parameter can be reduced by using a combination of different techniques, such as laboratory experiments, full scale experiments, and process modeling.

the uncertainty in predicting the performance of an ozonation treatment system is large, and that it is difficult to estimate the relative contribution of the various factors that determine this uncertainty.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a systematic and thorough uncertainty analysis is essential for reliable model-based prediction in water engineering.
the uncertainty in model parameters is not a static property of a model but rather a dynamic one that depends on the stage of the design process and the available information.
a comprehensive uncertainty analysis is a necessary step in the process of model development and validation.
